samples.summary: `files list` "validate --type before the dry-run branch" ordering is asserted for docs and sheets-export but not for files
samples.evidence: The diff adds the same ordering-sensitive comment/branch to files.ts:82-93 as to docs.ts:74 and sheets-export.ts:41. read-dry-run.test.ts has 'rejects an invalid --type BEFORE the dry-run branch' (line 121, docs) and 'rejects an unsupported --file-format BEFORE the dry-run branch' (line 192, sheets export), but the `files` entry in the describe.each block (lines 202-228) only runs `files list --dry-run` with no --type at all. If the dry-run branch were moved above the BLOB_TYPES check in files.ts, nothing in the suite would fail.
searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/*.ts for a files-list test

samples.summary: Segment encoding added to the `sheets import --dry-run` preview URL has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes sheets-import.ts:80 to `/documents/${seg(docId)}/tabs/${seg(localOpts.tab)}/cells`. There is no sheets-import test file (glob of packages/cli/test/*.ts shows none), and read-dry-run.test.ts registers only docs/notes/slides/files/api-keys/cells/sheets-export — never registerSheetsImportCommand. Reverting the `seg()` calls there would not fail any test.

samples.summary: Encoding of the `cells set` / `cells delete` / `cells batch` dry-run previews is untested
samples.evidence: cells.ts lines 66, 99 and 147 now wrap docId/tab/ref in `seg()`, but read-dry-run.test.ts only exercises `sheets cells get` (lines 145-178), and no other test file covers the cells command (grep for dryRun in packages/cli/test lists only slides-import, tabs, docs-import, files-upload, notes-import, read-dry-run). The write-path previews could silently regress to unencoded interpolation.
searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/*.ts for a cells test

samples.summary: Only 6 of ~17 newly-encoded HttpClient methods are covered by the new encoding test
samples.evidence: http-client-paths.test.ts exercises getDocument, deleteDocument, getCell, getCells, listTabs, getDocContent and revokeApiKey. The diff also adds `seg()` to updateDocument, putDocContent, get/putSlidesContent, get/putNoteContent, createTab, renameTab, setCell, deleteCell and batchCells — none of which any test calls, so the encoding on the mutating paths (the ones where a retargeted credentialed request is most damaging) is unguarded against regression.

samples.summary: The duplicated `seg` in dry-run.ts and http-client.ts is never asserted to agree; the preview-equals-request invariant is checked for exactly one command
samples.evidence: dry-run.ts exports its own `seg` while http-client.ts keeps a private copy. read-dry-run.test.ts line 267 checks the preview for `docs get ../../../admin` and http-client-paths.test.ts line 48 checks the real request for `../../../admin/users` — two separate tests over two separate implementations with different inputs. No test compares a printed dry-run URL with the URL the real client would fetch for the same arguments, so the two could drift (e.g. one switching to `encodeURI`) with the suite green.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts and http-client.ts seg definitions

samples.summary: The sheets-export invalid-format test does not assert a failure exit code
samples.evidence: 'rejects an unsupported --file-format BEFORE the dry-run branch' (lines 192-199) asserts stdout is empty and stderr matches /Unsupported format/, but unlike the analogous docs test at line 127 it omits `expect(process.exitCode).toBe(1)`, so a regression that printed the error yet exited 0 would pass.

samples.summary: `apiKeysUrl`'s `seg(keyId)` encoding is exercised only with a benign id
samples.evidence: api-keys.ts:15 encodes the key id in the preview URL, but the only revoke dry-run test (read-dry-run.test.ts:243) uses 'key-1', which encodes to itself. Dropping `seg()` from apiKeysUrl would leave the suite green even though http-client-paths.test.ts asserts the live revoke path IS encoded — exactly the preview/request divergence the change says it is preventing.
